newsitem.title: MEXICO: New owners take over Mexican Pacific-North railway.
newsitem.headline: New owners take over Mexican Pacific-North railway.

text.p: Mexican builder Empresas ICA said on Monday it was officially granted the 50-year concession for the Pacific-North railway, along with partners Grupo Mexico and U.S. Union Pacific.
The Pacific-North railway, about 3,900 miles (6,251 km) long, carries an estimated 40 percent of Mexico's rail cargo. In 1995 its revenue was 1.54 billion pesos.

Under the concession terms, the consortium called Grupo Ferroviaria Mexicana (GFM), also gained control Monday of 100 percent of a Pacific-North appendage, the Ojinaga-Topolobampo line, and a 25 percent stake in the Mexico City railway network, ICA said in a statement.
"With its participation in the railroad concession, ICA looks to reach its goal of having a third of its income from infrastructure operations," the company said.
The railroad operating company is led by Grupo Mexico, which holds a 74 percent stake. ICA and Union Pacific each hold a 13 percent stake in GFM.
The group paid $527 million for the concession, and has pledged to invest another $400 million over five years in the railway.
